Subject: MedSafe compute architecture: deal-aligned sizing & procurement path

Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a first-pass comparison of two deployment architectures that meet your regulatory constraints (data residency, SOC2-like logging, and contract-level auditability): Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated reserved GPU pools) vs Private (customer-managed private deployment/VPC with on-prem option). I attached the spreadsheet with assumptions and a high-level cost model.

High-level recommendation summary (TL;DR):
- For the Q1 pilot (30k monthly inference sessions, median prompt length ~120 tokens): Dedicated reserved capacity with a small private control plane gives the fastest time-to-value and simplest procurement path.
- For full production (3.5M monthly inference sessions, peak concurrency ~1.2k): Private (customer-managed deployment) lowers sustained unit cost by ~18–22% if you can accept a 6–9 month procurement and setup window.

Sizing snapshots (rounded):
- Dedicated (hosted, reserved): 12 reserved A100-equivalent slots (8 baseline + 4 burst). Expected 99th p95 latency < 400ms for typical chat workload; supports seamless fallback to smaller quantized variants.
- Private (on-prem or colocation): Equivalent of 9 H100-class nodes (3 racks with 3 nodes each) tuned for 16-bit quantization; better sustained throughput but longer provisioning and ops burden.

Key tradeoffs to call out:
- Procurement and timeline: Dedicated can be provisioned and tested within 3–5 weeks (contract + onboarding). Private typically requires 14–26 weeks (hardware purchase, network, KMS/HSM integration).
- Compliance controls: Both designs support audit logs, KMS integration, and tenant segmentation. Private gives strongest physical control and airgap options.
- Cost: Upfront capital for Private vs committed monthly for Dedicated. See attached cost model for 36-month NPV comparison.

Next actions I propose:
1) You confirm pilot target metrics (monthly sessions, SLOs for p95 latency).
2) We'll run a short benchmark (2 days) on a mirrored dataset in our Dedicated sandbox to validate latency and concurrency assumptions.
3) Parallel prep: procurement checklist and a Private deployment runbook if you want to accelerate to on-prem after pilot.

Attachments: medsafe_compute_req_v2.xlsx (assumptions + sizing), cost_model_draft.pdf (36-month draft model).

If helpful I can also sketch a three-phase procurement path (pilot -> hybrid short-term reserved+private prep -> full private migration) — that is what the attached sheet's tabs show.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call this week to walk through line items.

— Priyom

Priyom —

Thanks for the quick note and the attachments. A few clarifying Qs from our side after skimming the sheet:

1) Burst behavior: How do you handle spikes above the 4 burst slots in Dedicated? Can we autoscale into a higher-cost burst pool or fall back to a quantized model during spikes? We need a clear SLA for degradation behavior.
2) Data residency: For the Dedicated approach, is the data plane physically in our requested region (us-east) and can logs be pushed to our KMS?
3) Procurement timeline: Our procurement team wants a rationale for choosing Dedicated vs Private (they prefer CAPEX but IT is wary of ops load). Have you seen customers take the hybrid path you mentioned?

Also, budget heads-up: procurement has a 90-day window for capital approvals. If we go Private we likely won't make their deadline for this fiscal quarter.

Can you include an explicit three-option procurement ladder (Pilot Dedicated -> Hybrid reserved + Private prep -> Full Private) with clear milestone gates and decision criteria? That will help us present to IT and procurement.

Appreciate it — cc'ing Samantha as she'll own the procurement coordination.

Alex / Samantha —

Appreciate the quick follow-up — below is an explicit, short three-option procurement ladder plus concrete answers to your questions. I kept each item bite-sized so you can paste into the procurement memo.

Three-option procurement ladder (milestones, rationale, decision gates):

1) Pilot (Recommended near-term: Dedicated reserved + private control plane) — timeline: 3–5 weeks
- Scope: 30k monthly sessions pilot, baseline 8 reserved A100-equivalent slots + 4 burst slots.
- Deliverables: benchmark report, audit-log export, KMS integration proof-of-concept, SOC-like evidence pack.
- Gate to next phase: pass performance (p95 < 450ms), security signoff on audit logs and KMS.

2) Hybrid runway (Intermediate: extend Dedicated + start Private prep) — timeline: months 1–3 after pilot
- Scope: Maintain baseline reserved capacity; begin hardware procurement + network provisioning for Private.
- Deliverables: Private deployment runbook, network diagrams, HSM/KMS orchestration, DR plan.
- Gate to next phase: procurement approval + successful pilot de-risking (cost per inference within 10% of model).

3) Full Private (Final: customer-managed deployment) — timeline: 4–7 months from procurement start
- Scope: 9 H100-class nodes (3 racks) or equivalent colocation footprint; Redwood provides private control plane + managed onboarding.
- Deliverables: handed-over ops runbook, monitoring/tracing hooks, on-call rotation handoff if desired.
- Decision criteria: long-term unit cost targets (>=18% savings vs Dedicated NPV), IT signoff on ops and security.

Answers to your specific Qs:
- Burst behavior / autoscale: Dedicated supports two burst modes — autoscale into a short-term burst pool (higher per-token rate) OR graceful fallback to a quantized variant we maintain for you. Typical latency impact when falling back to INT8-like quantized model: p95 increases ~10–30% for chat (< ~100ms on top of baseline depending on prompt). For 2x spikes we expect p95 to remain < 650ms with autoscale; at 3x spikes we recommend intelligent throttling + quantized fallback to keep user experience acceptable.
- Data residency / KMS: Dedicated instances can be pinned to us-east region. We support customer KMS integrations (via bring-your-own-key) and provide audit log exports to your secure S3 bucket or push to your SIEM.
- Hybrid examples: Yes — multiple regulated customers have taken pilot -> hybrid -> private path; they'll typically commit to 6–12 months of Dedicated while hardware is procured and validated.

Commercial / SLA notes:
- We can offer a pilot-favorable credit (up to 30% of pilot fees) if you sign a 12-month runway at pilot start and commit to a three-month notice for migration to Private.
- SLA exceptions: for regulated workloads we can add enhanced logging retention and a 99.5% uptime SLA for reserved pools (subject to contract). Credits tied to missed SLOs are negotiable for enterprise terms.

Attached: medsafe_compute_req_v2.xlsx (updated to include the three-option ladder) and cost_model_draft.pdf (reworked NPV under hybrid trajectory). Also added a one-page procurement blurb you can paste into the CAPEX request. Link to internal case: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SALE-7842 and shared drive folder above.

If you want I can schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk the procurement blurb with your IT and procurement folks.
